look_here_first: Inspect the spurred yellow flower from the side, then compare mature capsules and seeds with C. micrantha. Golden corydalis typically has 13–16 mm flowers, and its fruits may spread or hang and curve; seed margin and fruit position depend on subspecies, so neither alone is decisive.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Approved source pool; Texas occurrence/native range supported at state scale; project three-county native criterion not certified.

morphology_keys.habit: Small, often spreading to ascending, delicate annual or biennial herb with multiple slender stems.
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate, petiolate, finely divided two to three times into rounded or oval ultimate segments; often bluish green.
morphology_keys.flowers: Bilateral, yellow, four petals, one outer petal with a rearward spur; racemes of several to many flowers; corolla often about 13–16 mm including 4–5 mm spur.
morphology_keys.fruits: Slender capsules about 15–25 mm, spreading to pendent or sometimes erect depending on subspecies; mature seed and capsule characters important.
best_field_traits: Side view of flower showing spur and crest
Mature capsule angle and shape, interpreted with subspecies variation
Seed size and marginal ring under magnification
Flower raceme relative to nearby leaves, not alone

comparisons.key_distinctions: Compared with C. micrantha, C. aurea often has slightly larger flowers and seeds and may show spreading or pendent capsules. C. micrantha often has erect, relatively straight capsules and cleistogamous flowering branches. C. aurea subsp. occidentalis can also have erect capsules and elevated racemes; use multiple characters, especially mature seed details.
comparisons.cautions: C. aurea subspecies differ in fruit angle, seed marginal ring and raceme height; do not identify solely by these characters or by yellow flower color. C. curvisiliqua subsp. curvisiliqua is a reference concept requiring careful taxonomy mapping, not a separate card in this batch.
